mainTopic: Mixed-up blood of the פר and שעיר on יום הכיפורים, what happens to unused blood (שירים or דחויין), and mixing the bloods for the corners of the inner מזבח
overview: This amud continues the discussion of the blood sprinklings inside the היכל on יום הכיפורים. The כהן גדול sprinkles the blood of the פר first and then the blood of the שעיר. רבא gives the correct order to follow when the two bloods got mixed together. The גמרא then covers two more cases: if the cups were switched, he sprinkles three full sets, and if some blood stayed unmixed, he simply uses the blood whose identity is certain. Next it asks whether the unused mixed blood is שירים, which goes to the יסוד, or דחויין, which goes to the אמה. רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע take opposite sides on this. Their debate rests on a ברייתא in which the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון disagree about blood left in unused cups, and רב אשי explains what 'its blood' excludes. Finally, the גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה, where the blood of the פר is poured into the blood of the שעיר. It shows that the משנה follows רבי יאשיה, who holds that the bloods are mixed before being put on the corners, and that ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא's corrected procedure for mixed blood
steps.stepSummary: רבא replaces the earlier rejected answer. The כהן גדול gives seven downward sprinklings for the פר, then one upward and seven downward for the שעיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: He sprinkles seven times downward for the bull. Then he sprinkles once upward and seven times downward for the goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא tells us an earlier suggestion was rejected. רבא now gives his own procedure for when the blood of the פר and the שעיר got mixed together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each animal needs one upward and seven downward sprinklings, done in order: first the פר's, then the שעיר's. רבא's procedure finishes the פר's set with seven downward sprinklings. Only after that does he do a complete set (one upward, seven downward) for the שעיר. This keeps the required order and avoids the problem that sank the earlier proposal.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the previous answer is rejected and a new one is coming.
Downward. These are the seven lower sprinklings.
Upward. This is the single upper sprinkling.
With intent for the bull
With intent for the goat

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think he sprinkles from two separate blood sources here. In רבא's case the blood is already mixed in one place. What makes the sprinkling count for the פר or the שעיר is the intent (לשם) and the order.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
He presents seven downward for the purpose of the bull,
and he again presents one upward
and seven downward for the purpose of the goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces a procedure the גמרא rejected on the previous amud.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Seven downward for the פר, then one upward and seven downward for the שעיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a mixture, finish the פר's sprinklings first, then do a full set for the שעיר.

steps.title: New case: the cups got switched
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new situation. The two cups, one with the פר's blood and one with the שעיר's blood, got mixed up, so he doesn't know which is which.
steps.simpleTranslation: What if the cups became mixed up with each other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new case. It is not answered yet; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This differs from step 1. There, the blood itself was mixed together. Here, each cup still holds pure blood, but we don't know which cup belongs to the פר and which to the שעיר. Since the פר must come first, picking a cup at random could get the order wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Became mixed or confused
Cups with cups, meaning the cups were swapped or confused

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with blood mixed into blood (step 1). Here nothing is blended. Only the identity of the cups is unknown.

phrases.english: If the cups became mixed with cups for him —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from mixed blood to switched cups.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to sprinkle in the right order when the identity of each cup is unknown.

steps.title: Sprinkle three full sets
steps.stepSummary: He sprinkles from one cup, then from the other, then again from the first. That is three sets in total, which guarantees a correct פר-then-שעיר order.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sprinkles, then sprinkles again, then sprinkles again: three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the switched-cups case. He does three full sets of sprinklings, going back and forth between the two cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the first cup was the פר's. Then sets one and two are correct, and the third does no harm. Suppose instead the first cup was the שעיר's. Then that first set doesn't count, because the שעיר came before the פר. In that case sets two (פר) and three (שעיר) are in the correct order. Either way, he has fulfilled his obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes back and presents again
Three times

steps.whatToRemember: When the cups are confused, three sets of sprinklings (A, B, A) guarantee that a valid פר-then-שעיר sequence happens.

phrases.english: he presents, and again presents,
and again presents, three times.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹתֵן, וְחוֹזֵר וְנוֹתֵן, וְחוֹזֵר וְנוֹתֵן, שְׁלֹשָׁה פְּעָמִים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three sets: first cup, second cup, first cup again.

steps.title: Partial mixture: use the blood that is certain
steps.stepSummary: If only some of the blood got mixed and some stayed unmixed, the answer is obvious. He sprinkles from the blood whose identity is certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: If some of the blood got mixed and some did not, it is obvious: when he sprinkles, he sprinkles from the blood that is certain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more case and closes it right away with פשיטא, meaning this one needs no discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If clearly identified, unmixed blood of each animal is still available, there is no doubt to solve. He simply uses the certain blood and ignores the mixed portion. The tricky procedures above are only needed when no certain blood remains.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of, some of
It is obvious
Certain, of known identity

steps.whatToRemember: The special procedures are only needed when no certain blood is left. If certain blood exists, he uses it.

phrases.english: If part of the blood became mixed for him,
and part of the blood did not become mixed [for him],
it is obvious: when he presents —
he presents from the certain blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְצָת דָּמִים נִתְעָרְבוּ לוֹ, וּמִקְצָת דָּמִים לֹא נִתְעָרְבוּ לוֹ, פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third case and dismisses it as obvious.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When certain, unmixed blood is available, he sprinkles from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When some blood stayed unmixed, he sprinkles from the blood of certain identity (מוודאין יהיב).

steps.title: What happens to the mixed blood that was not used?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the status of the mixed blood that the כהן גדול did not use. Is it שירים that goes to the יסוד, or דחויין that goes to the אמה?
steps.simpleTranslation: However, those other cups: are they leftover blood that goes to the base of the altar? Or perhaps they are rejected blood that goes to the water channel?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 4 settled which blood he sprinkles. Now the גמרא asks a new question: what does he do with the mixed blood he did NOT use?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, blood left over after a חטאת is sprinkled is called שירים, and it is poured on the יסוד (the base of the מזבח). Blood that was disqualified is called דחויין, and it is simply spilled into the אמה, the water channel that drains out of the עזרה. The question is which of these two categories the unused mixed blood falls into.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover blood after the required sprinklings; it is poured on the base of the מזבח
The base of the מזבח
Rejected or disqualified blood
The water channel in the עזרה that drains out to the נחל קדרון
Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)

phrases.english: However, those others: are they leftover blood,
phrases.notes: הָנָךְ = the mixed cups that were not used for sprinkling.

phrases.english: and so they go to the base of the altar,
or perhaps they are rejected blood,
and so they go to the water channel?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיהוּ, הָנָךְ: שִׁירַיִם הָווּ, וְלִיסוֹד אָזְלִי, אוֹ דִילְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question that grows out of the partial-mixture case in Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the unused mixed blood counts as שירים (goes to the יסוד) or as דחויין (goes to the אמה).

steps.title: רב פפא: the unused blood is rejected
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that even the view that one cup makes the other cup into שירים only applies when the second cup could have been used. Here it could not be used, so it is rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Even according to the one who says that one cup turns its partner cup into leftover blood, that only applies where the כהן could have used the second cup if he wanted. But here, where he could not use it even if he wanted, it does not become leftover blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. He says the unused mixed blood is דחויין and goes to the אמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known dispute about what happens when blood of one קרבן was caught in two cups and only one cup was used. One view holds that the second cup becomes שירים. רב פפא says that even this view only applies when the second cup was fit to be used. Mixed blood of uncertain identity could never have been used, so it cannot become שירים, and it is דחוי.

keyTerms.meaning: One cup turns its partner cup into leftover blood
This applies only (introduces a limit on a rule)
If he wanted to use it, he could have

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Even according to the one who says
that one cup makes its partner into leftover blood —
this applies only where
if he wanted to put it on, he could put it on.
But this case,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי בָּעֵי לְמֵיתַב לָא מָצֵי יָהֵיב — לָא.
phrases.english: where even if he wanted to put it on he could not — no.
phrases.notes: Meaning: it does not become שירים, so it is rejected and goes to the אמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כּוֹס אֶחָד עוֹשֶׂה חֲבֵירוֹ שִׁירַיִם
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mixed blood is דחויין, because it was never usable. So it goes to the אמה.

steps.title: רב הונא: on the contrary, the unused blood is leftover
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע flips רב פפא's reasoning. Even the view that one cup makes the other דחוי only applies when the כהן actively rejects it. Here no one rejected it, so it is שירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said to רב פפא: On the contrary! Even according to the one who says that one cup makes its partner rejected, that only applies when he rejected it with his own hands. But where he did not reject it with his own hands, it is not rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע argues against רב פפא and reaches the opposite conclusion: the unused mixed blood is שירים and goes to the יסוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא takes the opposite side of the same dispute about two cups. The other view holds that the second cup becomes דחוי. He limits that view to a case where the כהן actively pushes the blood aside, a דחייה בידים. Here the blood was never pushed aside by any act. So even that view would not call it דחוי, and it remains שירים.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary (introduces the opposite argument)
One cup makes its partner cup rejected
He rejected it with his own hands, through a direct act

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the reversal. רב פפא and רב הונא each take the view that seems to work against them and limit it. רב פפא ends up saying the blood is דחוי (goes to the אמה). רב הונא ends up saying it is שירים (goes to the יסוד).

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rav Pappa:
On the contrary:
Even according to the one who says
that one cup makes its partner rejected —
this applies only where he rejected it with his hands,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלָא דַּחְיֵיהּ בְּיָדַיִם — לָא.
phrases.english: but where he did not reject it with his hands — no.
phrases.notes: Meaning: it is not דחוי, so it is שירים and goes to the יסוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא: אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer and gives the opposite ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב פפא's conclusion that the unused mixed blood is דחוי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Rejection requires an active act. Blood that was merely unusable, without being pushed aside by hand, is not דחוי.

steps.title: The ברייתא behind the two-cups dispute begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that compares two פסוקים: one says 'its blood' and the other says 'all its blood.' This is the source of the dispute about two cups.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Above, the פסוק says 'and he shall pour its blood,' and below, it says 'and he shall pour all its blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It begins quoting the ברייתא that is the source for the dispute about whether one cup makes the other שירים or דחוי. The derivation itself continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק (ויקרא ד:כה, the שעיר of a נשיא) says just 'its blood.' The second פסוק (ויקרא ד:ל, the חטאת of a commoner) adds the word 'all.' That extra word 'כל' is what the ברייתא will use to learn the rule about blood left in a second cup.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall pour out (the leftover blood at the יסוד)
All its blood; the extra word 'כל' is the key to the derivation

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya depends on how this extra word 'כל' is read. That reading decides whether the second cup counts as שירים or as דחוי.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Above it says:
"And its blood he shall pour out" (Leviticus 4:25),
and below it says:
"And all its blood he shall pour out" (Leviticus 4:30).
phrases.notes: That extra word 'all' is exactly what the ברייתא is learning from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that is the source for the 'one cup makes its partner' dispute that both אמוראים referred to.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute over whether one cup makes its partner שירים or דחוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא comparing ויקרא ד:כה ('its blood') with ויקרא ד:ל ('all its blood').

steps.title: Blood sprinkled from each of four cups all goes to the base
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. If blood of a חטאת was collected in four cups and one sprinkling was taken from each cup, the leftover blood in all four cups goes to the יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that if a חטאת's blood was collected in four cups, and the כהן sprinkled once from each cup, all of the leftover blood is poured on the base of the מזבח? The פסוק says: 'And all its blood he shall pour.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the ברייתא it began quoting in the last step. Here it gives the first case: every cup was used once, so every cup's leftover blood is שירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'all its blood' (כל דמה) teach that the leftovers of all four cups count as שירים and go to the יסוד. This works because every cup took part in the sprinklings.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering
Cups or bowls used to collect blood
The base of the מזבח, where leftover blood is poured
'And all its blood he shall pour'. The פסוק that includes every cup

phrases.english: From where do we know regarding a sin-offering
that he collected its blood in four cups
and sprinkled once from this one and once from that one,
that all of them are poured on the base?
The verse says: 'And all its blood he shall pour.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִין לְחַטָּאת שֶׁקִּבֵּל דָּמָה בְּאַרְבַּע כּוֹסוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that step 8 began quoting.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute over whether one cup makes another cup into שירים or דחוי

steps.title: If all sprinklings came from one cup, only that cup goes to the base
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא limits the first rule. If all four sprinklings came from one cup, only that cup is שירים for the יסוד. The other cups are poured into the אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that even if he did all four sprinklings from one cup, all the cups go to the base. So the פסוק says: 'And its blood he shall pour.' That cup is poured on the base, and the other cups are poured into the drainage channel.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now uses the second פסוק, 'its blood,' to set a limit. Unused cups do not count as שירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Its blood' (דמו) narrows the rule to the cup that was actually used. The unused cups are treated as rejected (דחויין) and go to the אמה. This is the view that one cup can push another cup aside.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think'. Introduces a mistaken idea that the פסוק will correct
Sprinklings of blood
The drainage channel in the עזרה, where rejected blood goes
'And its blood he shall pour'. The פסוק that limits the rule

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the view that an unused cup becomes דחוי. That view sits behind the debate between רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע earlier.

phrases.english: One might think: even if he sprinkled
four sprinklings from one of them
The verse says: 'And its blood he shall pour.'
That one is poured on the base,
and they (the other cups) are poured into the channel.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ נָתַן אַרְבַּע מַתָּנוֹת מֵאַחַת מֵהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 9 by using the second פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The view that an unused cup becomes דחוי

steps.title: רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון says all four cups go to the base
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees. Even if all four sprinklings came from one cup, all the cups are שירים and go to the יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון says: From where do we know that if a חטאת's blood was collected in four cups, and he did all four sprinklings from one of them, all of them are poured on the base? The פסוק says: 'And all its blood he shall pour.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא in the same ברייתא gives the opposite ruling about the unused cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון reads 'all its blood' to cover even the cups that were never used. In his view, one cup turns the others into שירים, not into rejected blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Are poured out
Leftover blood after the sprinklings, which goes to the יסוד

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים quote the same words 'all its blood' (כל דמה). The difference is the case: the תנא קמא applies it only when every cup was used, while רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון applies it even when only one cup was used.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Shimon says:
From where do we know regarding a sin-offering whose blood he collected
in four cups
and he sprinkled four sprinklings from one of them,
that all of them are poured on the base?
The verse says: 'And all its blood he shall pour.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's limit in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even unused cups become שירים and go to the יסוד.

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון do with 'its blood'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון. The פסוק 'its blood' seems to limit the rule, so how does he explain it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון, isn't it written: 'And its blood he shall pour'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון deals with the פסוק the תנא קמא used to exclude the unused cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא used 'its blood' to send the unused cups to the אמה. If רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון does not accept that, the פסוק still needs some purpose in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But it is written'. Raises a פסוק that seems to contradict a view

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Shimon,
isn't it written: 'And its blood he shall pour'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view stated in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'its blood' seems to limit which blood goes to the יסוד. That contradicts including all the cups.

steps.title: רב אשי: 'its blood' excludes blood left in the animal's neck
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that 'its blood' excludes blood that comes out of the animal's throat after the blood was collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It comes to exclude leftover blood that is in the animal's neck.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון a different use for the limiting פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון, 'its blood' does not exclude unused cups. Instead it excludes blood that was never collected in a cup at all, such as blood that drips from the neck afterward. That blood is not שירים and goes to the אמה.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude
The animal's neck or throat

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree that 'its blood' excludes something. The תנא קמא excludes unused cups. רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון excludes only blood left in the animal's neck.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
To exclude the remainder
that is in the neck of the animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לְמַעוֹטֵי שִׁירַיִם שֶׁבְּצַוַּאר בְּהֵמָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the פסוק a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Its blood' must exclude unused cups, which would contradict רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Its blood' excludes blood left in the animal's neck, so all collected cups can still be שירים.

steps.title: The משנה follows the view that the bloods are mixed for the corners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which says the blood of the פר was poured into the blood of the שעיר. It notes that this follows the view that the two bloods are mixed before being put on the corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He poured the blood of the bull into the blood of the goat.' We learned this משנה like the one who says the bloods are mixed for the corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה. It identifies which opinion the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before putting blood on the corners of the inner מזבח, the משנה has the כהן גדול combine the פר's blood with the שעיר's blood. That shows the משנה holds the bloods are mixed, not applied separately.

keyTerms.meaning: He poured from one vessel into another
The bull and the goat of יום כיפור
They mix the bloods
The corners of the מזבח

phrases.english: He poured the blood of the bull
into the blood of the goat.
We learned this like the one who says:
They mix the bloods for the corners.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵירָה דַּם הַפָּר לְתוֹךְ דַּם הַשָּׂעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows the view that the bloods are mixed before being put on the corners.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן argue about mixing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the dispute it just referred to. One of רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן says the bloods are mixed, and the other says they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן. One said they mix, and one said they do not mix.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source of the dispute to back up its last statement. It is also setting up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We are not told which of the two holds which view. The משנה sides with the one who says the bloods are mixed. The other view holds that each blood is put on the corners separately.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One said'. The opinions are given without saying who holds which

phrases.english: As it was stated:
Rabbi Yoshiya and Rabbi Yonatan,
one said: they mix,
and one said: they do not mix.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the dispute that step 14 referred to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is disputed whether the bloods of the פר and שעיר are mixed before being put on the corners.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה must be the one who requires mixing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רבי יאשיה is the one who says to mix the bloods. This fits his general rule that two items named in one פסוק count as joined, even without the word 'יחדיו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can conclude that it is רבי יאשיה who says the bloods are mixed. He holds that even when the word 'together' is not written, it is treated as if it were.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to work out which of the two תנאים says the bloods are mixed. It suggests רבי יאשיה, based on how he reads פסוקים in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה has a general rule: when a פסוק lists two things, they are treated as one combined unit, as if 'יחדיו' were written. Our פסוק says 'of the blood of the פר and of the blood of the שעיר'. By his rule the two bloods form one unit, so they are mixed. רבי יונתן holds the opposite rule (each item stands alone unless 'יחדיו' is written), so he would seem to say they are not mixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Conclude / we can settle that (the גמרא proposes an identification)
They mix (the two bloods together)
Together (a word that joins two items in a פסוק)
It is as if it were written

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'יחדיו' does NOT appear in our פסוק about the blood. The point is that רבי יאשיה treats the פסוק as if it did say 'together', because it names two things side by side.

phrases.english: Conclude that it is Rabbi Yoshiya
phrases.notes: The גמרא is suggesting whose view this unnamed opinion is.

phrases.english: who says that they mix (the bloods),

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא כְּתִיב ״יַחְדָּיו״
phrases.english: for he says: even though 'together' is not written
phrases.notes: His general rule for reading פסוקים.

phrases.english: it is as if 'together' were written.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה הוּא דְּאָמַר מְעָרְבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 15 left open which תנא holds which view. This step tries to settle it using רבי יאשיה's general reading rule.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יאשיה is the one who requires mixing the bloods.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יאשיה's known general rule that two items in one פסוק are treated as if 'יחדיו' were written.

steps.title: Even רבי יונתן could require mixing because the פסוק says 'once'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Even רבי יונתן might require mixing here, because the פסוק says 'אחת', meaning one single application.
steps.simpleTranslation: You could even say this is רבי יונתן's view. Here is different, because it is written 'once'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from Step 16. It shows that even רבי יונתן could agree to mix the bloods in this specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן normally treats two items in a פסוק as separate. But a different פסוק about the inner מזבח says 'אחת' (once), which teaches that the blood is put on only one time. To put it on only once, the two bloods must already be mixed. So mixing here comes from the word 'אחת', not from רבי יאשיה's general rule, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: You could even say (a pushback against a proof)
Here is different (this case has a special reason)
Once / one time (from the פסוק about atonement on the corners of the inner מזבח)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a general reading rule may not decide a case if a special word in the פסוק points to the same result for a different reason.

phrases.english: You could even say it is Rabbi Yonatan,
here it is different, since it is written: 'once'.
phrases.notes: That's the פסוק in שמות ל:י: 'וכפר אהרן על קרנתיו אחת בשנה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 16 by giving רבי יונתן a separate source for mixing.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof that mixing must be רבי יאשיה's view. It does not prove that רבי יונתן actually holds this.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 16 assumed mixing could only come from the 'as if יחדיו' rule. But the word 'אחת' could require mixing even according to רבי יונתן.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms that רבי יאשיה is the one who mixes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted that goes against the pushback in Step 17. It says clearly that the פסוק teaches mixing, and that this is the view of רבי יאשיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that goes against our answer: 'And he shall take of the blood of the פר and of the blood of the שעיר' — this teaches that they must be mixed. These are the words of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that undoes its own pushback. The ברייתא names רבי יאשיה as the one who learns mixing from this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 suggested that even רבי יונתן might mix, because of 'אחת'. The ברייתא instead learns mixing from the words 'of the blood of the פר and of the blood of the שעיר' and credits it to רבי יאשיה alone. That fits the identification in Step 16. The ברייתא continues on the next amud with רבי יונתן's opposing view.

keyTerms.meaning: Not like our answer (against the pushback we just gave)
Mixed together

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יאשיה says the bloods of the פר and שעיר are mixed before being put on the corners, learned from 'וְלָקַח מִדַּם הַפָּר וּמִדַּם הַשָּׂעִיר'. The משנה follows רבי יאשיה. The ברייתא is introduced as going against the 'אחת' answer, and its continuation on the next amud gives רבי יונתן's opposing view.
steps.confusionAlert: 'דלא כשינויין' means the ברייתא goes against the גמרא's own answer (Step 17), not against the משנה. It actually supports the first idea in Step 16.

phrases.english: It was taught (in a baraita) not in line with our answer:
'And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat',
phrases.notes: This פסוק is in ויקרא טז:יח.

phrases.english: that they should be mixed; these are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undoes the pushback of Step 17 and brings back the identification made in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the mixing view belongs to רבי יאשיה and is learned from 'מדם הפר ומדם השעיר', not from 'אחת'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that quotes ויקרא טז:יח and credits mixing to רבי יאשיה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה, which has the blood of the פר poured into the blood of the שעיר, follows רבי יאשיה.
